text: Given your significant alcohol consumption, I need to assess for liver involvement. Do you have any pain or tenderness in your upper right abdomen, or have you noticed any swelling in your legs or abdomen?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your jaundice, weight loss, and smoking history, I am concerned for pancreatic or biliary pathology. REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT abdomen and pelvis is normal, I need to evaluate for hepatocellular causes or extrahepatic compression. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests

text: RESULTS: AST: Elevated, ALT: Elevated, ALP: Significantly elevated, Bilirubin: Elevated

text: The significantly elevated alkaline phosphatase suggests cholestasis, so I need to visualize the bile ducts. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging of the abdomen and bile ducts, I suspect an infiltrative process within the liver itself. REQUEST TEST: Liver Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since imaging and biopsy are normal, I suspect a systemic or vascular cause. Do you have any shortness of breath, chest pain, or swelling in your legs? REQUEST TEST: Doppler Ultrasound of Hepatic Veins

speaker: Doctor
text:
With normal imaging, biopsy, and vascular studies, the combination of alcohol use, smoking, weight loss, and cholestatic labs points to an infiltrative process like alcohol-associated hepatitis with steatosis or early primary biliary cholangitis, but given the context, I will diagnose Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease
